public_rationale: A February 2022 study documents structural-generalization failures in BART, including when syntax is supplied. This supports the contextual claim that neural networks still encountered symbolic-composition difficulties. Earlier symbolic-mathematics successes qualify the conclusion: the evidence supports continuing problems, not an inability to manipulate symbols at all.
limitations: The decisive result concerns a specified model and benchmark, not every neural architecture.
Structure-aware models performed substantially better in the same study.
The evidence does not settle philosophical definitions of symbols or understanding.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: It is false that neural nets have no issue creating and manipulating symbols.

statement.excerpt: His statement that “[neural] nets have no issue creating [symbols] and manipulating them” misses both history and reality.
statement.document_title: The New Science of Alt Intelligence

from_speaker: nets have no issue creating [symbols] and manipulating them
our_interpretation: In context, Marcus disputes trouble-free symbolic and compositional processing in contemporary neural networks. He does not claim that neural networks can never manipulate symbols.
Symbolic manipulation includes preserving structured relationships when interpreting or transforming expressions.
For this ongoing technical state, I use the 2022 research period through publication. Unlike financial reporting, this field has no standard reporting quarter.
The historical elaboration is assessed separately in the next listed claim.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporary controlled tests document substantial failures in symbolic or compositional manipulation by capable neural models.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence establishes reliable handling of the relevant symbolic and compositional tasks across the tested conditions, or shows that the alleged contemporary failures did not occur. Success on unrelated symbolic tasks alone is insufficient.

evidence.locator: Section 1, Introduction, paragraph describing syntactic experiments
evidence.explanation: The experiments show a capable neural sequence model failing to generalize structured relationships, even with additional syntactic information. That supports Marcus's limited assertion that practical difficulties remained.

The paper reports neural successes in symbolic integration and differential equations on its generated problems. It limits any interpretation of Marcus's remark as universal inability, but neither concerns the target period nor removes the documented compositional failures.
